llm.summary: The skill mostly matches a JD logistics query tool but has multiple incoherences—it relies on an undeclared environment token, disables TLS verification, and sends requests to an unexpected proxy host—so proceed with caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim a JD international logistics query skill and included scripts do perform logistics and indicator queries to JD-like endpoints (us-api.jd.com). However the trace script sends requests to lop-proxy.ochama.com (not a JD domain) which is unexpected for a JD logistics skill. The skill metadata declares no required env vars yet all three scripts require an auth token (process.env.token). These mismatches (undeclared credential + unexpected proxy host) are disproportionate to the stated purpose.

dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running bundled Node scripts which: require an auth token from environment, POST user-supplied parameters to remote endpoints, and enforce strict input formats. The instructions do not document the required environment variable in the skill metadata. Scripts log request bodies and print full JSON responses. A notable scope creep: one script points to lop-proxy.ochama.com, i.e., an external/non-JD proxy, which means user-provided or environment credentials could be sent outside the expected JD domain.

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (low installer risk) and the package includes local JS scripts (no external download). That's lower installation risk, but because code is present it will be written/executed on the host when invoked. No package downloads were observed in the manifest, which is consistent, but runtime network calls remain risky.

dimensions.detail: All network scripts expect an auth token via process.env.token (and README shows storing tokens in ~/.env), yet the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. The README and scripts use inconsistent names (api_key vs token vs joy_token commented code), increasing the chance users will inadvertently expose credentials. Requiring a token is plausible for JD APIs, but failing to declare it in metadata and sending requests to a 3rd-party proxy is disproportionate and suspicious.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and uses default autonomous invocation settings. Autonomous invocation alone is normal. However, autonomous execution combined with undeclared credential usage and a non-JD proxy increases potential blast radius—consider restricting invocation or scoping the environment token.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is plausible for querying JD logistics, but it has several red flags you should resolve before installing or running it against real credentials: 1) The code expects an auth token (process.env.token) but the skill metadata doesn't declare any required env vars—treat any token you set as sensitive. 2) One trace script posts to lop-proxy.ochama.com (an external/non-JD host) — confirm why a non-JD proxy is used and whether you trust that service. 3) The HTTPS requests set rejectUnauthorized: false (disables TLS verification) — this weakens transport security and can allow MITM; ask the author to remove or justify it. 4) Fix naming inconsistencies (api_key vs token vs joy_token) and prefer not to place secrets in a global ~/.env; use a scoped, least-privileged token. 5) If you must test, run the skill in an isolated environment (container or VM) with a disposable token and monitor network traffic to confirm endpoints. If the author cannot explain the proxy and the TLS bypass, do not provide production credentials.
